precepts.text: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness. Every one of them is dross and tin. All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.
precepts.point: Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and her converts with righteousness. And the destruction of the transgressors and of the sinners shall be together: wicked Israel gets the same judgment as Esau. They shall be ashamed of the oaks which ye have desired: the idols. Confounded for the gardens that ye have chosen: the churches. As an oak whose leaf fadeth: your understanding is gone. As a garden that hath no water: no water of understanding. And they shall both burn together, and none shall quench them: God gets rid of what he cannot use.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
“And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin.” Dross is waste, refuse, any worthless matter, and the tin goes with the dross. God will turn his hand upon us, the Israelites, and purge away everything within us that is wasteful and useless. What is that? Christ lists it.

“For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts”: from within, out of the mind of men. Evil thoughts: that is dross and tin. “adulteries, fornications, murders, Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness”: every one of them is dross and tin. Add the rest we carry: lying, stealing, child molestation, masturbation, pornography, bestiality, anger, malice. All of it.

“All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.” The dross is not outside of us; it is in us, and that is what God is purging.

So that one verse speaks volumes. The “thee” God turns his hand upon is you and me, and what he purges away is everything that proceeds out of our own hearts and defiles us, so that afterward Israel can be called “The city of righteousness, the faithful city.”

precepts.text: We glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience. When you read Paul in Hebrews 12, nobody rejoices in tribulation, but he gives you the after effect. When you go through hell, you learn patience; and patience, experience: a lot of us come into this truth with experience in the world but no experience in the truth of God. And experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed, because we endure to the end. That tribulation goes back to Ecclesiasticus 2: when thou comest to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.

precepts.why:
For the dross to be purged away, we have to go through some things. Paul shows it: “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also.” When you read Paul in Hebrews 12 he tells you nobody rejoices in tribulation, but here he gives you the after effect. Why glory in tribulation? “knowing that tribulation worketh patience.” That tribulation goes back to Ecclesiasticus 2: when you come to serve the Lord, prepare your soul for temptation, the hard times. When you go through hell, you learn patience.

“And patience, experience.” Patience gives you experience. A lot of us come into this truth at 30, 40, 50 with experience in the world, but in the truth of God we have no experience. That is the experience we need.

“and experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed.” Experience teaches us hope, and hope makes us not ashamed, because we endure to the end, “because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.”

So the purging of Isaiah 1:25 is done through tribulation. God turns his hand upon us, and what we go through works patience, experience and hope in us, until the dross and the tin are gone.

precepts.text: But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth. The great house is the nation of Israel, the twelve tribes. In every school there are men and women who are gold and silver, and it is up to you to discern who they are; and in every school there are also brothers and sisters of wood and of earth. This is not about new brothers and sisters who just walked through the door: it is about men and women in this truth for years who have not changed, still murmurers and gossipers, no work, no effort to study, treating this like a social club, a place to hang out. If a man therefore purge himself from these: you have to know your circle. When the Bishop came into the truth he had a circle of brothers he was always in trouble around, and he had to change his circle and get around leadership and the elders to get his mind right. Do not worry about hurting feelings: if you know they are not right, separate from them. Then shall you be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use: then can God use you, send you to a city and you could grow a whole congregation. Like Isaiah said to the Lord: send me. And this is also why we cannot join with other camps that practice what God condemns: it is based on what we just read.

precepts.why:
God will “purely purge away thy dross.” Paul uses that same word, purge. “But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver.” The great house is the nation of Israel, the twelve tribes. We are not speaking for the other camps, with their cookouts on the Sabbath, their raping of girls, their stealing money for Maseratis and beating the baby mothers; we speak for Israel United in Christ. In every IUIC school, Philly, DC, Virginia, New York, Atlanta, Connecticut, OKC, there are men and women who are gold and silver, and it is up to you to discern and identify who they are.

“but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” In every school there are also brothers and sisters of wood and of earth: they are not right. This is not about new brothers and sisters who just walked through the door; we all walk in not right. It is about men and women in this truth for years who have not changed: still murmurers and gossipers, putting forth no work and no effort to study and improve. To them it is a social club, a place to hang out with the homeboys, drink a little wine, then go home and play dominoes. The vessels of dishonor are here to try you, and every bird clings to its like; see who groups together.

“If a man therefore purge himself from these”: you have to know your circle. When the Bishop came into the truth he had a circle of five or six brothers he was always getting in trouble around, down to jumping the turnstile with them and getting a ticket. He had to change his circle and get around leadership and the elders to get his mind right. Don’t worry about hurting feelings; if you know they are not right, separate from them.

“he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.” Then God can use you. Then we can send that brother to a city or a state and he can grow a whole congregation, like Isaiah telling the Lord, send me.

And this is why we cannot join with the other camps: it is based on what we just read. Only a fool would do that. The same purging God does in Isaiah, we must do ourselves.

precepts.text: Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil. Once you got water baptized, you were supposed to put off the evil of your doings. The church has not figured that out; they think there is power in the water itself, but if nothing changes in you, you just went in wet and came out wet.
precepts.point: Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him through the faith of the operation of God. Baptism was always symbolic: you are buried in the water as in the grave, and you come up a new creature.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
“Buried with him in baptism, wherein also ye are risen with him.” Baptism was always symbolic. Isaiah says what the washing was for: “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil.”

So by water baptism, wash you, make you clean, put away the evil of your doings. Once you were water baptized, you were supposed to put off the evil of your doings. You are buried in the water as in the grave, and you come up a new creature. That is the symbolism behind it.

“Cease to do evil.” The church has not figured that out yet. The Christian church thinks there is power in the water itself, that when you come out of the water you will no longer be a crackhead or a homosexual. No: if nothing changes in you, you went in and you came out wet. That is all. The change is in putting away the evil of your doings, not in the water.

precepts.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Heavy laden with sin, and the rest is not a good night's sleep: it is the kingdom, rulership for a thousand years under Christ. This is why we need a saviour; we cannot do it without Christ.
precepts.point: They have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward. That is why we went into captivity: Deuteronomy 28:15 through 68 laid out the curses for breaking the commandments, and many of us are still moonwalking away from the Most High. Now is our time to get our minds right and repent.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Isaiah calls us “a people laden with iniquity.” Christ answers that very word: “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” Heavy laden with what? With sin, the iniquity Isaiah just named.

That is why we are in need of a saviour. We read the history of our forefathers in the wilderness: the Most High showed great signs and wonders, and we were still a stiff-necked, hard-headed people. We are “a sinful nation”, “a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters.” We forsake the Lord every time we sin, and we have “provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger.” That is why the so-called blacks and Hispanics went into captivity, just as Deuteronomy 28:15 through 68 laid out the curses for breaking the commandments. Many of our brothers and sisters are still going backward, moonwalking away from the Most High. Brothers and sisters, we cannot do it without Christ.

So be honest and sincere, even in prayer. Do not go to the Most High acting righteous when you are full of dead bones, sin and guile. None of us is righteous; we are trying, but there is sin still in us. Open your mouth and confess the things you are battling with.

“and I will give you rest.” That rest is not a good night’s sleep. It is our land, the kingdom of God, rulership for a thousand years under Christ. That is the true rest he is talking about, but we have to come unto him. Now is our time to get our minds right and repent.

precepts.text: Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings. That is the true washing: cease to do evil, learn to do well. Action, not speech. Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; if ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land, but if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword.
precepts.point: Who did the healing? The spirit of Christ, working through Elisha. What healed Naaman was his belief and his obedience to the word of the prophet.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Naaman was told, “Wash, and be clean”, and when he believed and obeyed the word of the prophet, he was clean. Isaiah shows what the true washing is: “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil; Learn to do well”.

Put away the evil of your doings: that's the true washing. Cease to do evil, learn to do well. Action, action, action. Not speak well, do well. “seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.”

“though your sins be as scarlet”, bloodshot red, “they shall be as white as snow”, if you learn to do well. “though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.” But it hangs on obedience: “If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land: But if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword”.

That is Naaman. At first he refused and went away in a rage. When he humbled himself and did according to the saying of the man of God, his flesh came again like the flesh of a little child. His belief and his obedience are what made him clean.

precepts.text: Ah sinful nation, a seed of evildoers who revolt more and more; the whole head is sick and there is no soundness from the foot to the head, wounds not mollified with ointment: no healing but the Saviour.
precepts.point: Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity, Miss Laura included, and all that prey upon thee shall be a prey. For I will restore health unto thee: only the Lord heals, by Christ's stripes, for they that are whole need no physician and he came to call sinners to repentance. Because they call thee an outcast, African-American, Haitian, Jamaican, this is Zion whom no man seeketh after.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
“Thy bruise is incurable, and thy wound is grievous. There is none to plead thy cause, that thou mayest be bound up: thou hast no healing medicines.” None stands up on our behalf, and we have no healing medicine. Every Negro that just popped out of his mama's behind has a new idea for how to save black people, and it is always economics or voting. Those medicines don't work. What is the wound? Our sins. Isaiah says the same thing.

“Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.” We are that sinful nation, a people laden with sin; iniquity is sin. He calls us a seed of evildoers.

“Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more”. Our people get punished and revolt more and more against God. Then: “the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint”: the whole head of the Israelites is sick.

“From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.” Neither mollified with ointment means no medicine: there is no healing for us that way. That is Jeremiah's “no healing medicines.”

The only one who can save us is the Saviour, Jesus Christ, our master, our king. Yes, he is our rabbi, and rabbi means master. The wound Jeremiah calls incurable is incurable by any remedy of men; only the Lord can say, “I will restore health unto thee”.

precepts.text: I will purge away thy dross and restore thy judges as at the first: everything returned to our glorious state.
precepts.point: The whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury and falls upon the head of the wicked, and the fierce anger of the Lord shall not return until he hath performed the intents of his heart; in the latter days ye shall consider it.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
“Their children also shall be as aforetime, and their congregation shall be established before me”. The Lord is going to return it all back to the way it was.

Isaiah says the same: “And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin:” “And I will restore thy judges as at the first”. He purges the dross out of Israel and restores the judges as at the first, the way it was in the beginning.

That is what Jeremiah 30:20 is saying: our children as aforetime, our congregation established before the Lord, everything returned to our glorious state. And it answers verse 21 too, “their nobles shall be of themselves”: our own judges, restored as at the first.

precepts.text: Woe to them that sin, and keep not my commandments. Sin is not keeping God's commandments. Put this in your arsenal beside 1 John 5:3; precept upon precept.
precepts.point: The whole head is sick. You are sick and I am sick. That is the whole point of the class: we have to keep getting right.

note.label: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

precepts.why:
Isaiah cries, “Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity”. We are laden: like a ladle dipped in soup, we are soaked and drenched with iniquity. A sinful nation means we break God's laws. So what is sin? Ezra answers: “Woe to them that sin, and keep not my commandments! saith the Lord.”

Sin is when we don't keep God's commandments. Brothers, put this in your arsenal. We always go to 1 John 5:3, of course, but we have to understand that it is precept upon precept, and Ezra says the same thing.

And who are the people that were given God's commandments? The twelve tribes of Israel. That is who Isaiah is calling the sinful nation. He was never talking about the Hittites or anybody but the Israelites.

This matters now because wars are here, and it is no time to think you are ready. You may wear your fringes, keep your beard right, keep the Sabbath and put the pork down, but still battle with patience, anger, a brawling spirit, an evil eye, or the weed you won't put down. Woe to them that sin. The whole head is sick: you're sick and I'm sick, and we have to keep getting right.

precepts.text: He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel; he hath not dealt so with any nation. The commandments were given to the twelve tribes, and Israel is the nation that gets judged. That is why our people went into the trans-Saharan and trans-Atlantic slave trades.
precepts.point: The whole head is sick. You are sick and I am sick. That is the whole point of the class: we have to keep getting right.

note.label: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

precepts.why:
Isaiah says the sinful nation has “provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger”. To prove which nation that is: “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel.” Jacob was the forefather of the twelve tribes, and his name later became Israel. The statutes and the judgments were given to the nation of Israel.

“He hath not dealt so with any nation”. So for modern-day Christians to say that God is dealing with all nations and all people, they don't know the Bible.

Then: “and as for his judgments, they have not known them.” The Israelites are the ones that get judged. That is why Black people went into slavery, in the trans-Saharan slave trade and the trans-Atlantic slave trade, and many other times in history we have served our enemies in slavery.

So Isaiah was never talking about anybody but the Israelites. We are the seed of evildoers who call evil good and good evil, led astray by Christian pastors and the leaders in the mosques. From 1865 to 1965 we lived under more overt racism, but we had civility, women had a dress code, and there was an order to talk to a sister. Since 1965 we have gained almost twenty million abortions by Black women alone and the dumbest generation of children with the smartest technology. We provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, and that is why we went into slavery.

precepts.point: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh, the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee, thy tabernacle shall be in peace, and thou shalt not sin: Isaiah 60:21 says thy people shall be all righteous. Thy seed shall be great as the grass, and thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age like a shock of corn in its season: Israel's life will be long, forever.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
Job 5:18: “For he maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole.” He makes us sore, and Isaiah 1 shows where we are bruised from the top of our head.

“Ah sinful nation”: that is us, you and me. “A people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters”: we are the corrupters. “They have forsaken the Lord”: our people have forsaken the Lord. “They have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward”: we have gone backwards from God’s laws.

“Why should ye be stricken any more?” God is saying, I keep punishing you over and over, why should you be stricken any more? “Ye will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint. From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.”

In Isaiah 1:4-6 he is talking about us in comparison with Job. Job was real, don’t get it wrong, but his life represents the nation of Israel. He lost everything, even his health, from the top of his head to the soles of his feet, and that is what Isaiah says about the nation of Israel as a whole. But the same God that “maketh sore” also “bindeth up”; “his hands make whole.” He will make us whole again.

precepts.text: Had I sent thee to them of a strange speech, they would have hearkened unto thee.
precepts.point: The ox knoweth his owner, but Israel doth not know. Ask the nations who they are and they know their village; Israel gives a hundred answers.

note.label: 2025 Recap: Different Times, Same Truth

precepts.why:
“The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master’s crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.” The Israelites are the only people on the face of the earth who do not know who they are. Ask around and you get a million answers: black, colored, African-American, Nuwabian, the Asiatic black man, Muslim, Christian, we are all one in Christ. Ask a white man and he is Polish; others can trace their lineage back to the village their ancestors came from.

“my people doth not consider”: not only do we not know who we are, we do not even consider that we could be the people of this book. We have been teaching it for forty years, and now there are urban apologists whose whole life is set around proving us wrong. We are the only people who will fight not to be God’s chosen. On a show like The Bachelor all the nations would run to be the bride of Christ, with the promises and the covenant; black people are the only ones saying, Don’t nobody want him.

Ezekiel shows it: “Not to many people of a strange speech and of an hard language, whose words thou canst not understand. Surely, had I sent thee to them, they would have hearkened unto thee.” God did not send the prophet to a people of a hard language. If he had, they would have hearkened in a heartbeat.

That is how we know we are the people. We have the best videos, the best music, the best teachers; the Bishops and Deacons broke the book down precept upon precept from the first book to Revelation, as no pastor in the history of Christianity ever touched, and still the negro says, Nah, I’m good, what about John 3:16? The other nations would hearken. Israel doth not know and doth not consider.

precepts.text: I will restore thy judges as at the first.
precepts.point: After Adam transgressed, the ways became narrow, and Israel must now labour for the inheritance.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Ezra is shown “A city is builded, and set upon a broad field, and is full of all good things”, with an entrance so narrow that only one man can go at once. That city is the kingdom of heaven, our inheritance: “Even so also is Israel's portion. Because for their sakes I made the world”. When Adam transgressed, the entrances were made narrow, full of sorrow and travail. But “the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure”. The elder world is the old world, the kingdom of Adam, where all of us were with him, ruling.

Isaiah shows the Lord bringing that back: “And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city.”

As at the first: that is the elder world, when Adam was ruling. There were judges set up then, and the twelve tribes of Israel were set up with him at that time, ruling with him. Were we in the flesh back then? No; we were immortal. As at the beginning: the beginning is Genesis.

So the Lord is not only promising good rulers again. He is promising to restore the government of the old world, the judges and counsellors we had in the beginning, and to call that city the city of righteousness. That is the city full of all good things that Ezra saw, and it is Israel's portion.

precepts.text: Wash you, make you clean; cease to do evil is how you are made clean.
precepts.point: No surgery can circumcise the brain: circumcision of the heart is repentance. You wash you and make you clean by ceasing to do evil, and a young man cleanses his way by taking heed thereto according to the word of the Most High.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
No surgery can circumcise the brain: circumcision of the heart is repentance. “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil”. You wash you and make you clean by ceasing to do evil.

That is the spiritual circumcision the flesh points to. The men of Joshua's day applied the law of circumcision as a form of repentance; the heart is circumcised by putting away the evil of your doings.

precepts.text: Zion, the Israelites, shall be redeemed with judgment and her converts with righteousness, but the transgressors and sinners that forsake the Lord shall be consumed together.
precepts.point: Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and to be converted you have to be keeping God's laws, His righteousness. When you forsake the Lord's laws you are consumed together with the sinners.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Let the redeemed of the Lord say so, whom he hath redeemed from the hand of the enemy”. Isaiah tells who the redeemed are and how they are redeemed: “Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and her converts with righteousness.”

“And the destruction of the transgressors and of the sinners shall be together, and they that forsake the Lord shall be consumed.” When you forsake the Lord's laws you are consumed together with the sinners. The redeemed are the ones that did not forsake him.

points: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz concerns Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah. These are the days in which Isaiah prophesied.

Isaiah was a servant and prophet during Hezekiah's reign, before the Assyrian captivity destroyed the nation. The split between the northern and southern kingdoms had already come, going back to Solomon's idolatry and the friction between Rehoboam and Jeroboam.
Isaiah is a heavy, prophetic book; even the Ethiopian eunuch was reading Isaiah when the spirit sent Philip to help him understand it.

note.label: Isaiah 1: A Sinful Nation, Yet Zion Redeemed With Judgment

points: "Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth: for the LORD hath spoken." The Most High nourished and brought up children, and they rebelled against Him; this is the nation of Israel.

note.label: Isaiah 1: A Sinful Nation, Yet Zion Redeemed With Judgment

points: The ox knows its owner and the ass its master's crib, but Israel does not know and does not consider. These dull animals still know where they live and who owns them, so that Israel does not is a hard but constructive rebuke.

note.label: Isaiah 1: A Sinful Nation, Yet Zion Redeemed With Judgment

points: "Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters": the nation is covered in sin because it loves what America and the traditions of men have taught, such as keeping Valentine's Day, which traces back to the pagan Lupercalia. They have forsaken the law, the good doctrine of Proverbs 4:2, and provoked the Holy One of Israel to anger, gone away backward.

note.label: Isaiah 1: A Sinful Nation, Yet Zion Redeemed With Judgment

points: The Most High asks, "Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more." Like bad children who only get worse the more they are punished, Israel keeps rebelling under affliction, whether earthquakes in Haiti, hurricanes in Puerto Rico and Florida, crime, or prisons filled with His chosen people, and revolts further into unnatural states.

The whole head is sick and the whole heart faint. The head being sick is the leadership; thanks are given that the southern kingdom's bishops, elders, deacons, and captains are waking up, or the nation would be sicker still.

note.label: Isaiah 1: A Sinful Nation, Yet Zion Redeemed With Judgment

points: "From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it, but wounds, and bruises, and putrefying sores." From the least tribe to Judah and the southern kingdom the nation is wounded, and the sores are not closed, bound up, nor mollified with ointment. The ointment that heals, whether physical or spiritual, is the word of the Most High.

note.label: Isaiah 1: A Sinful Nation, Yet Zion Redeemed With Judgment

note.label: Isaiah 1: A Sinful Nation, Yet Zion Redeemed With Judgment
